data.title: Enel Buys Portfolio of U.S. Solar Plants From energyRe
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Enel agreed to buy a portfolio of solar plants in the U.S. from clean energy infrastructure developer energyRe, part of a strategic plan to grow generation capacity from renewable sources.

The Rome-based energy company said Friday that the plants, located in South Carolina, have a total installed capacity of 317 megawatts and an expected average annual production exceeding 540 gigawatt-hours.

Following completion and once the plants are in service, Enel expects the deal to boost its annual group earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization by around $30 million, while its total North American installed capacity of 13.5 gigawatts will come entirely from renewable sources.

Acquisition terms weren't disclosed, but Enel said that coupled with the costs of bringing the plants into service, it expects the deal to have an impact on group net financial debt of around $255 million.

Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

data.title: MoonPay applies for national trust bank charter to expand stablecoin services
data.description:
Crypto payments firm MoonPay announced Thursday it had filed an application with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to launch MoonPay National Trust Bank.

The application, dated Nov. 17 and received by the OCC on Nov. 18, said MoonPay's trust bank would provide fiduciary custody services; stablecoin services, including issuance, redemption, and reserve management; and conversion services as an agent.

The filing is to organize MoonPay National Trust Bank as a non-depository national bank, limited to trust company operations and related activities. It would not seek federal deposit insurance and would operate as a member bank of the Federal Reserve.

If approved, the national charter would provide a single federal framework for MoonPay to offer custody and stablecoin-related services. MoonPay’s application comes ahead of the GENIUS Act taking effect on Jan. 18, 2027, when payment stablecoin issuers will generally need approval under the new framework.

Applying for OCC approval

Several other major crypto firms have received full or conditional approval for the same type of OCC national trust bank charter.

Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to Circle (CRCL), Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Paxos. Circle received final approval in July 2026, while Ripple received its full approval in October. Coinbase's (COIN) became effective earlier this month. Additional firms, including Stripe's Bridge, Crypto.com, and World Liberty Financial, hold conditional approvals.

Meanwhile, MoonPay has expanded its regulated and enterprise footprint over the past year. It received its New York BitLicense in June 2025 and its New York trust charter in November 2025.

Earlier this year, MoonPay agreed to acquire private markets platform North Capital in an all-stock deal. It launched enterprise stablecoin services in November 2025 and partnered with WisdomTree to incorporate a tokenized Treasury fund into stablecoin reserves. It has also announced a strategic collaboration with Dunamu, the parent company of South Korean crypto exchange Upbit, to explore stablecoin-based global payments and fund movement.

Former Commodity Futures Trading Commission Acting Chair Caroline Pham also joined MoonPay as chief legal officer and chief administrative officer last December.

data.title: RBI eases forex reporting norms for small service exporters, importers; sets Rs 10 lakh threshold for EDF filing
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has clarified foreign exchange reporting requirements for exporters and importers of services under its new trade regulations, following amendments that exempt resident individuals and certain small-value transactions from separate documentation requirements.

In FAQs published on November 20, the central bank clarified that service exporters other than resident individuals need to file an Export Declaration Form (EDF) only when the value of an inward remittance exceeds Rs 10 lakh, or its equivalent in foreign currency. Resident individuals are exempt from separate EDF filing irrespective of the value of the inward remittance.

The clarifications explain changes introduced through the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026, notified on November 2 and made effective retrospectively from October 1.

The broader regulations, issued in January 2026, replaced the earlier framework and consolidated more than 150 RBI circulars, with the objective of simplifying compliance and delegating operational responsibilities to authorised dealer (AD) banks.

What the November amendment changes

The November 2 amendment introduced the definition of a 'resident individual', specifying it as a person resident in India who is a natural person.

It also amended the EDF requirements for service exports. Under the revised provisions, a resident individual is deemed to have submitted the EDF once the required information relating to the receipt of payment is provided to the authorised dealer for crediting the export proceeds.

The same treatment applies to service exporters other than resident individuals if the inward remittance does not exceed Rs 10 lakh.

The amendment also narrowed the reporting requirement for imports of services. Authorised dealers are now required to enter import-of-service details in the Import Data Processing and Monitoring System (IDPMS) within five working days only when the importer is not a resident individual and the invoice or contract value exceeds Rs 10 lakh.

EDF timelines and software exports

The FAQs clarify that non-individual service exporters receiving remittances above Rs 10 lakh must submit the EDF within 30 days from the end of the month in which the invoice is raised for software exports.

For other services, the form must be submitted within 30 days from the end of the invoice month or on or before receipt of payment. Authorised dealers can extend the submission deadline if they find the exporter's request reasonable.

The RBI has also discontinued the SOFTEX form from October 1. Software exporters operating in the domestic tariff area can now submit the EDF to any authorised dealer or the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI). Exporters operating from special economic zones can submit it to the respective Development Commissioner.

The central bank has further clarified that the earlier requirement for obtaining an EDF or Guaranteed Remittance waiver has been discontinued. Where exported goods have no realisable value, exporters must declare zero value in the appropriate field of the EDF. AD banks are no longer authorised to issue such waiver letters.

Banks to publish trade policies

The RBI has mandated authorised dealers to publish their trade-related policies and the main features of their standard operating procedures for handling trade transactions on their websites.

It has also clarified that transactions initiated before October 1 will continue to be governed by the earlier regulatory framework, even if they are completed after that date.

data.title: Gold slide deepens as market anxiety overtakes real-rate pressures
data.description:
Gold prices are tumbling as the Federal Reserve's aggressive rate-hiking cycle sparks a "fear factor" in markets that may be triggering a deleveraging wave, according to strategist Robin J. Brooks.

The unusual price action this week in precious metals comes alongside a sharp rise in the dollar against emerging markets, which Brooks describes as "usually an indication of deleveraging kicking in."

The Fed's hawkish stance is driving real Treasury yields to their highest levels in over two decades, creating significant headwinds for gold, the strategist explained. While falling oil prices have provided some support for the precious metal, that effect has faded now that Brent crude has settled in the low $90s per barrel. "The rise in real rates is certainly weighing on gold, but that effect is minor," Brooks said, noting that the more significant driver is market anxiety.

Non-linear moves in the dollar, gold, and copper are emerging even as real rates and oil prices have recently stabilized, suggesting that "stuff is breaking," according to Brooks.

His regression analysis of gold's daily price movements shows that the "fear factor" has been building since Fed Governor Waller began discussing 50-basis-point rate hikes ahead of last week's inflation data. "The fact that real rates in recent days stopped rising, even as gold has continued to fall, suggests that a fear factor is at play," he said.

Brooks warned that the Fed's hawkishness could prove self-defeating and may cause a market "accident." "Once deleveraging starts, unpredictable things can happen," he cautioned, adding that geopolitical risks involving Iran could further complicate the outlook.

The strategist called on Fed Chair Warsh to provide clearer forward guidance, arguing that internal squabbling should not "hold the US economy hostage."

data.title: AM Need to Know: Alibaba faces Megaspeed lawsuit, Nvidia eyes AI acquisition & more
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell early Friday as investors assessed the fallout from Wall Street's sharp selloff in the previous session, when major indexes tumbled more than 2% each.

Now, here are four news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:

Alibaba sued by shareholders over Megaspeed ties amid Nvidia spy scandal: Alibaba   faces a proposed class action lawsuit filed Thursday in Manhattan federal court, with shareholders alleging the Chinese e-commerce giant misled them by concealing connections to Megaspeed, a Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing access advanced Nvidia AI chips. The complaint claims Alibaba knowingly understated in its 2024, 2025, and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business. Shareholders cited Alibaba's relationship with Megaspeed, whose executive Alice Huang had a relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and reportedly helped move about 240,000 H100, H200, and A100 chips into China.

SpaceX sells $32 billion in off-balance-sheet AI chip debt above 8% yield: SpaceX sold $32 billion of bonds Thursday to fund its  purchase of artificial intelligence chips, in a transaction that may serve as a model for similar financings to come. The debt offering was designed to keep the borrowing off SpaceX's balance sheet and is part of a more than $40 billion financing that also includes bank loans. Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management ran the transaction, which will allow SpaceX to buy Nvidia chips that the company will lease for about five years.

Nvidia in advanced talks to buy AI startup Inception for over $500 million: Nvidia is in advanced discussions to  acquire Inception, a two-year-old AI startup developing diffusion-based large language models, in a deal valued at more than $500 million. The transaction would bring Inception's three co-founders—Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov—into Nvidia full-time. Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, Inception has more than 30 employees and previously raised $50 million from investors including Menlo Ventures, M12, Mayfield, and Nvidia.

U.K. retail sales volumes increase 2.3% Y/Y in October, topping estimates: U.K. retail sales volumes  rose 0.7% month-over-month in October, beating economists' expectations for no growth, according to data released by the Office for National Statistics. The increase followed a 0.4% decline in September. On a year-over-year basis, retail sales volumes rose 2.3%, accelerating from 0.8% growth in the previous month and exceeding consensus estimates of 1.7%. The stronger-than-expected reading points to an improvement in consumer spending, with both monthly and annual retail sales growth exceeding market forecasts.

data.title: US lawmakers near deal to ban Chinese cars, with potential exemption for Mercedes: report
data.description:
U.S. lawmakers are nearing an agreement on legislation to ban Chinese cars from the domestic market, with last-minute negotiations focused partly on protecting Mercedes-Benz , which is nearly 20% owned by Chinese entities, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Republican and Democratic lawmakers from auto-producing states aim to send the bill to President Donald Trump by year-end. The measure would further restrict Chinese automakers such as BYD and Geely from accessing the lucrative US market, which is already largely closed to them by tariffs and restrictions on Chinese vehicle technology.

Republican Senator Bernie Moreno briefed automaker representatives Wednesday on proposed changes to earlier legislation targeting Chinese connected vehicles. The revisions include provisions that could shield Mercedes from an outright ban, the people said.

Automakers were broadly supportive of the proposed changes, although a Mercedes representative raised reservations. Negotiations remain ongoing, with lawmakers hoping to pass the measure before the next Congress begins in January.

“We continue to meet with all stakeholders who have a shared interest in ensuring this important legislation becomes law in this Congress,” Mercedes said.

An earlier bill advanced by a Senate panel would have barred manufacturers more than 15% owned by Chinese entities from selling vehicles equipped with data-transmitting technology. Mercedes has lobbied for changes to the proposal. China's state-owned BAIC Motor owns nearly 10% of the German automaker, while Geely founder Li Shufu holds nearly another 10%.

Provisions under discussion include relaxing restrictions for companies with passive ownership stakes that lack voting rights, as well as ways to structure and verify such exemptions, the people said.

Republican Senator Katie Britt of Alabama, where Mercedes operates a major SUV production facility, said she had worked on the legislation with Moreno and believed both the automaker and the state would be protected.

“We understand that there will be some adjustments that have to be made, but feel good about Mercedes continuing to be able to thrive in our state and across the country,” she said.

US automakers such as General Motors , Ford and Tesla could benefit from reduced competition if Chinese automakers are further restricted from accessing the US market.

data.title: Premium flagship smartphone prices likely to go up by over 30% by year-end: Counterpoint
data.description:
Prices of premium flagship smartphones are expected to go up by 30 per cent to over ₹1 lakh apiece across most of the brands by end of the year due to a sharp rise in memory chip cost, market research firm Counterpoint said on Friday.

Along with the increase in prices of the devices, consumer expectations are also rising, and consumers are looking for meaningful specifications that can match the desired experience across processing speed of the mobile phones, camera, battery, durability, after-sales service, etc.

"A few years ago, a ₹1-lakh smartphone was a rarity in India. Today, as flagship prices keep rising, this price point is becoming increasingly common. Prices of premium flagship devices are expected to rise by more than 30 per cent by the end of 2026 compared with 2025," Counterpoint Research said in a report.

Memory prices are expected to account for 43 per cent of the total phone cost by year-end compared to 13 per cent in the first quarter of 2025, as per the report.

"Rising DRAM (temporary storage) and NAND costs, driven by AI data centre demand, have pushed memory's share of smartphone BOM (bill of materials) from about 13 per cent in early 2025 to over 40 per cent, prompting smartphone manufacturers to reassess specifications, components and product strategies to manage costs," said Tarun Pathak, Research Director, Counterpoint Research.

According to the report, Oppo flagship devices have seen the highest jump in the range of 82-87 per cent on a year-over-year (YoY) basis.

Ultra-premium segment market leader iPhone prices have gone up by 20-22 per cent YoY.

"There is no single best premium flagship, as consumer priorities vary. As Apple and Samsung flagship prices move towards Rs 2 lakh, tech-focused brands like iQOO and Google are attracting consumers with specifications that are at par but at more competitive prices. Beyond hardware, ecosystem flexibility is becoming an important differentiator, especially for working professionals who tend to carry more than one smartphone in addition to a laptop," the report said.

Market leader Samsung recently increased the price of smartphones in the range of ₹2,000-₹4,000 apiece post Diwali.

Before Diwali, the firm had raised the price of its flagship device Galaxy S26 by 17 per cent.

Chinese smartphone company Xiaomi has also increased the price of devices in the same range after Diwali.

data.title: Turkey Capacity Utilization Rate Falls Slightly; Business Morale Weakens Further
data.description:
ANKARA (dpa-AFX) - Turkey's manufacturing capacity utilization decreased for the first time in three months in November, while factory confidence worsened further to the lowest level in nearly two years, figures from the central bank showed on Friday.

The capacity utilization rate dropped to 74.4 percent in November from 74.5 percent in October.

The decrease in November was mainly due to lower utilization of durable consumer goods, which dropped to 67.7 percent from 68.5 percent. Capacity utilization for investment goods also declined to 72.5 percent from 73.4 percent, while that for intermediate goods rose slightly to 74.5 percent from 74.4 percent.

The confidence indicator for the manufacturing sector weakened to a 23-month low of 99.2 in November from 99.8 in September. Any score below 100 indicates a pessimistic outlook.

Employment expectations over the next three months weakened in November, with the corresponding index falling to 99.6 from 104.5 in October. The index measuring the current situation of the total amount of orders remained almost unchanged at 85.4, compared to 85.3 in October. However, the output expectations index improved to 109.2 from 107.0.

data.title: Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest — Update
data.description:
By Paul Hannon

Eurozone wage growth accelerated slightly in the three months through September, but remained modest despite the pickup in inflation triggered by the war between the U.S. and Iran.

The European Central Bank on Friday said wages negotiated by labor unions and similar groups were 2.57% higher in the third quarter than a year earlier, an increase in the annual rate of growth from 2.45% in the three months through June.

Since the start of the war, officials at the ECB have highlighted the outcome of wage negotiations as a key indicator as to whether the jump in energy prices triggered by the conflict is set to keep inflation above their 2% target.

But there are few signs as yet that workers are securing larger pay rises to cover increased energy bills.

"What we don't see at the moment is second-round effects, not yet," Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin said in an interview with CNBC on Thursday. "We need to be vigilant about what will happen and that's the reason we've increased rates in the past."

The ECB raised its key rate in September and June.

The eurozone's annual rate of inflation rose to 4% in October from 1.9% in February, the month in which the war began.

That pickup in the pace of price rises has weakened the spending power of eurozone households, and for the year as a whole the European Commission now estimates that wages adjusted for inflation will increase by just 0.4%, a sharp slowdown from 1.8% in 2025.

It expects real wages to rise at a similarly slow pace next year, with the commission forecasting that compensation per worker will rise at an unchanged pace of 3.5%.

data.title: Wall St futures slip as Anthropic debut fails to reassure AI investors
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures down: Dow 0.2%, S&P 500 0.76%, Nasdaq 1.63%
  • Anthropic down 6.5% a day after its debut
  • Gap gains on Old Navy recovery

US stock futures fell on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing could steady an AI trade rattled by growth and valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.

Anthropic shares slid 6.8% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.

The Claude chatbot creator's IPO was seen as a key test of investor confidence in the AI theme after a bruising few weeks for the sector. Concerns over potentially slower data center expansion, higher borrowing costs and the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have intensified fears about returns on massive spending.

The Nasdaq was 13.6% below its record closing high of October 6.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon , Meta , and Microsoft declined more than 1.8% each, while Alphabet was muted. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Chipmakers were lower, with Nvidia down 2.6%, while Advanced Micro Devices , Broadcom , Marvell , and Micron lost between 3.5% and 5.5%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius also dropped more than 5% each.

Data center stocks IREN , Applied Digital and Core Scientific fell between 2.8% and 4%.

At 4:57 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were down 99 points, or 0.2%, and S&P 500 E-minis were down 54.5 points, or 0.76%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 434 points, or 1.63%.

Wall Street's main indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% reported earnings above analyst expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.

Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Brent crude prices fell 1.6% and were heading for a third straight weekly loss on expectations of a supply surplus, with crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returning to roughly prewar levels.

Markets were also assessing the outcome of the meeting between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, after the leaders issued a joint peace declaration that made no mention of the conflict between the US and Iran.

Among other movers, apparel retailer Gap rose 2.5% after its Old Navy brand posted better-than-expected quarterly sales.
